author: David Reed
summary: chg-24 bounds submit_authorization's DB transaction to the work rather than the request. It had been held open across the Claude API calls (~23s), making SQLite concurrency literally 1, pinning a Postgres connection idle-in-transaction, and costing 55 audit rows to 'database is locked' in one clinical run. Also defines the duplicate-request_id contract, which previously returned an unhandled 500.

changes.description: Commit T1 (request write) before the LLM work and open a short T2 for the decision write, so no DB transaction spans the Claude API calls. Defines the duplicate-request_id contract: idempotent replay, 409 on a reused id carrying a different case, resume after a died attempt, 409 while an attempt is in flight.
changes.failure_pattern: A long-lived DB write transaction held open across an external network call. FastAPI's get_session commits at end-of-request, and this request makes 1-3 Claude calls in the middle, so the write lock taken at the request insert was held for the whole ~23s.
changes.root_cause: Transaction lifetime was coupled to request lifetime by the session dependency. Nothing in the route closed T1 before orchestrator.process_decision, so the lock, the connection and the open transaction spanned the LLM window.

evidence.note: Lock hold 0.5095s -> 0.0013s (SQLite) and 0.5436s -> 0.0026s (Postgres). engine.pool.checkedout() == 0 during the LLM window after the change.

SQLite N=10: 1/10 -> 10/10 completions, audit_write_failed 30 -> 0, wall 22.4s -> 0.61s. Postgres N=20 on pool 15: 15/20 -> 20/20, audit_write_failed 65 -> 0, wall 120.7s -> 0.91s. Independently reproduced by adversarial validation.
Verified by execution: a second submission with the same request_id hit the unique index and fell through to except Exception -> HTTP 500. There was no duplicate handling in the route at all.

predicted_fixes: T1 transaction hold drops below 10ms and N=10 concurrent SQLite submissions all complete. Measured true: 1-4ms, 10/10.
Zero audit_write_failed events under concurrency on both backends, because chg-23's independent audit session no longer competes with a long-lived writer.
No duplicate-request_id path returns 500. Same case replays idempotently with no new LLM call; a reused id carrying a different case returns 409 and never the stored decision.
risk_cases: Cross-patient decision leak on a reused request_id -- mitigated by a field-level check on patient_id/primary_diagnosis_code/treatment_code, proven capable of catching a naive replay implementation. It is NOT a payload fingerprint: a different case sharing those three fields would replay.

A duplicate arriving while the first submission is in flight produced two decisions and then permanently 500'd that request_id (found by adversarial validation, not by the suite). Mitigated by an age-vs-agent_timeout heuristic plus a decision lookup that can no longer raise on multiplicity.

The in-flight heuristic is a heuristic, not a lease. A request legitimately exceeding agent_timeout (60s) is misclassified as dead and resumed; conversely a genuinely dead request cannot be retried for up to agent_timeout because it still looks in flight. A claimed_at/worker_id lease column is the rigorous fix and needs a migration.
Replay asymmetry: a replayed decision always reports cited_evidence_ids == [] because no column persists it, so an EHR client diffing first response against replay sees that field differ.

Keeping the injected session rather than a session factory (a deliberate deviation, forced by ~24 existing tests that call the route function directly) left the resume path re-pinning a connection across the LLM call -- 0.5445s with checkedout()==1. Fixed with a path-specific commit; a session factory would have made the class structurally impossible.
changes.why_this_component: The defect is in the route's transaction management, not in any agent's reasoning, tool or prompt. agents/orchestrator.py was deliberately untouched. The harness taxonomy has no name for the request/persistence layer; tool_implementation is the closest fit and the gap is recorded rather than force-fitted.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert the chg-24 commits touching authorizations.py and repository.py. No migration, no schema change -- the status column already existed. The new test files can remain; they would fail against reverted code, which is useful signal.

verified_fixes: Boundary matrix through the real _call_with_retry: 500/503/504/529/599 retried to llm_retry_max_attempts; 499 and the full 4xx set attempted exactly once.

max_retries=0 on the client makes tenacity the sole retry authority: worst case for a persistent 5xx is exactly llm_retry_max_attempts HTTP requests under one visible schedule, down from up to 9 under two.
retry-after / retry-after-ms honoured and clamped to llm_retry_wait_max_seconds; a hostile 86400 clamps to 30s.
missed_fixes: Disabling the SDK retry loop initially discarded its retry-after handling -- a rate-limit regression traded for a visibility fix. Caught in review, not by any test, and restored at the tenacity layer in the same iteration.
verified_risks: MagicMock implements __float__ (returns 1.0), so an unconfigured mock header would have parsed as a real 1s retry-after and introduced actual sleeping into the suite. Guarded by an isinstance check; recorded as AGENT_LESSONS P-011.
verdicts.notes: Clinical gate passed 9/9 at the iter-16 merge HEAD; golden-set 87.2% (34/39), 0 hallucinations.

verified_fixes: A scope violation after the request row exists persists exactly one decision row and is returned by list_escalated_for_review().

The persistence audit across every escalation exit was independently re-derived by execution using total-table row counts: pre-flight, evidence-grounding, confidence branch 3, kill switch, Medical Director (both outcomes) and RAG-degraded all already persisted exactly one row.
The persist failure envelope covers SQLAlchemyError, so a database failure inside the handler is audited rather than escaping as an unaudited 500.
missed_fixes: The initial envelope caught only ScopeViolation and IntegrityError; an OperationalError from get_by_id escaped as an unaudited 500. Widened in the same iteration.
verified_risks: A violation on the db.write_decision action itself still never reaches the queue -- the re-guard deterministically re-denies. Correct fail-closed behaviour, audited as escalation_persist_failed, and recorded rather than left in a code comment.
verdicts.notes: The deliberate non-persist on a db.write_request-time violation was independently judged correct: persisting would perform the exact write the guard denied.

verified_fixes: On real Postgres 16: a normal successful request persists 7/7 route audit rows with request_id intact, and pre-write rows survive a business-transaction rollback. Both measured 0 before migration 007.
Live A/B on identical code proved migration 007 necessary rather than convenient: at 006 the same code persisted 0/7 with seven ForeignKeyViolationErrors; at 007, 7/7 with none.
Both original CRITICALs are structurally unreachable: the retry path is deleted, and the returned entry never enters a session so it cannot become detached.
missed_fixes: The independent audit session competes with the request's own long-lived write transaction on SQLite, costing 55 audit rows to 'database is locked' in one clinical run. Invisible on Postgres (MVCC) and not caught by any test -- surfaced by the clinical gate itself. Fixed by chg-24, which removes the long-lived transaction.
A non-AsyncEngine bind silently degraded the commit to savepoint semantics with zero error events -- a silent fallback in the lane whose purpose was eliminating silent failure. Now refused loudly.
verified_risks: Migration 007's downgrade is a one-way door on any Postgres database that has exercised rollback survival: orphaned request_id values are produced by design, so re-adding the FK fails. It fails safe (transactional DDL) and the cleanup procedure is documented in the migration.
unforeseen_regressions: The SQLite lock contention above. It is the clearest case this cycle of a fix whose cost appeared only on the backend its tests did not exercise -- recorded as AGENT_LESSONS P-009.
verdicts.notes: The first version of this change would have destroyed 7 of 7 audit rows per SUCCESSFUL request on Postgres while passing every SQLite test. Caught by adversarial validation against a real container, not by the 890-test suite.
